raw_graphql_pull_request.body:
## Overview

The Rust frontend already decoded `EngineCoreOutput.num_nans_in_logits`, but the value was discarded before request metrics were recorded. Consequently, `/metrics` did not expose `vllm:corrupted_requests_total`, even when engine-core detected NaNs in request logits.

Track corruption across the complete request lifecycle and export the request-level counter already provided by the Python frontend. This restores visibility into numerical corruption that may indicate model, kernel, or hardware problems.



## Claims



## Validation

```bash
cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets --all-features --locked -- -D warnings

cargo nextest run -p vllm-llm --test generate \
  generate_records_request_metrics_in_prometheus_output

cargo nextest run -p vllm-metrics -p vllm-llm \
  --all-features --locked --no-fail-fast
```



## Details



---

<summary> Pull Request Checklist </summary>

- [ ] I used vLLM's `/pr-checklist` skill. (Mandatory for agents, optional for humans).
- [ ] AI assistance was used during the creation of this PR.

- [ ] **Design Fit:** Minimizes impact on core components, reuses existing functionality, and justifies added complexity.
- [ ] **Testing and Validation:** Validates the change and ensures any added tests are meaningful and reliable, with CI coverage or documented CI resource constraints and validation performed outside CI.
- [ ] **Code Quality and Style:** Keeps code and comments clear and concise, and updates relevant documentation and examples.
- [ ] **Pull Request Contents:** Includes a brief summary and relevant links, supports claims with evidence, explains root causes and implementation trade-offs, and follows the contributing guide.
</details>
